task: First paid GPU invocation of assistant-llm-v2
result: vLLM never served a request. --enable-sleep-mode switches vLLM onto the cumem allocator, which invalidates its memory profiling: it sized a 13.77 GiB KV cache then died with CUDA Error: out of memory at cumem_allocator.cpp:163, reporting 24.29 GiB allocated by PyTorch on a 22.06 GiB card. Container exited code 1 after 212.2s; Modal restarted it, and the retry was stopped with modal app stop -y. Roughly 6 A10 container-minutes spent for no measurement. No snapshot created, no cold-start number exists. Confirmed working for the first time: the snapshot machinery engaged (Creating GPU memory snapshot for Function), the bounded readiness wait reported the exit code instead of hanging, proxy auth accepted Modal-Key/Modal-Secret on a .modal.run endpoint, and max_containers=1 held. head: e54bb669d7dce29b817d5e4987069bbdc1b88d61
task: Chromium, a persistent workspace and document reading for roadmap queue 1
result: The worker and self_test run on an agent_image that adds chromium and fonts; the webhook stays on the smaller layer. Browser launch flags are read from the machine, so a container gets no-sandbox and a desktop keeps the browser sandbox. A Modal volume gives each person a workspace that outlives the container, reloaded before and committed after every turn. A document is saved into that workspace and read with a new read_document tool over pdf, docx, md, txt and csv, keeping page and section labels; a scanned PDF is reported as a scan rather than as empty. Approved by the human in words: volume instead of sandbox for persistence, and save-then-read instead of extract-at-admission. Nothing deployed, so no capability here is accepted yet.

head: e54bb669d7dce29b817d5e4987069bbdc1b88d61
task: Look at a PDF page instead of recognising it
result: Tried the browser route first and measured it: headless Edge does render a file:// PDF legibly, but returns the viewer's toolbar and scrollbar in the frame, one page at a time, over a scheme inspect_page blocks, and Debian chromium's PDF viewer was never established to exist. Chose pypdfium2 instead, approved by the human. view_pages renders a page to a PNG with nothing but the page in it, long side 1400 px, at most two per call because the server accepts four images per prompt. No OCR: the multimodal model looks at the page. A page of 11-point text was rendered and read back legibly. /check gained documents.view; all four free probes pass locally.

head: e54bb669d7dce29b817d5e4987069bbdc1b88d61
task: Stop the assistant denying it can look at, or show, a document
result: Found live: asked to show the PDF it had just summarized, the assistant answered it is a text model with no way to display anything. Two causes. The generated capability brief said documents are 'never shown to you directly' and did not mention view_pages - a hand-written sentence inside the one artifact that is generated so it cannot be wrong. And _deliver returned early for any tool message, so a rendered page reached the model and stopped at the adapter. The brief, the tool description and the system prompt now cover being asked to look at or show a document, and a tool's media is delivered to the chat while its text still is not. Approved by the human. Not yet redeployed.

The capability brief, the system prompt and the tool description now all state that the person receives the same picture and that calling the tool is what sends it. The old delivery sentence said only never tell the person you can only output text, which was true and not the sentence the model needed. Not deployed. A clean retest needs /new because the failing thread contains the earlier denial.

head: f9edc7ca6f42256b8b64501f22be7bade533f0c4
task: Fix five review findings on the web capability (SSRF pinning, browser request filtering, overall timeout, prompt honesty, screenshot budget)
result: fetch_page now connects to the validated IP with Host and SNI preserved, closing DNS rebinding for the fetch path, and address checking consults is_global as well as the named properties so 100.64.0.0/10 is refused. Every request the browser makes is intercepted through CDP Fetch and put through the same check, verified live by a redirect into 169.254.169.254 failing with ERR_ACCESS_DENIED. The whole fetch loop runs under one asyncio deadline. Web guidance moved from DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT into the generated capability brief, so a grant that withholds a tool no longer leaves the prompt advertising it. Screenshot pruning now applies the declared budget. Interception introduced a CDP id collision that emptied every rendered page's text; found by rendering real pages, fixed, and the view probe now requires the text as well as the PNG.
